# "The Damned Fourth" 4th Hazardous Operations Company, USCM Hazardous Operations Unit
The [bold]Hazardous Operations Unit[/bold] of the USCM specializes in high-risk environments, including chemical, biological, radiological, and explosive threats. HAZOPS teams are trained for rapid response and containment in CBRN conditions.
## Overview
The United States Colonial Marine Corps’ Hazardous Operations Unit, often abbreviated to HAZOPS, was formed on May 2nd, 2162. HAZOPS was formed due to rapidly increasing construction of large colonies, research facilities, and industrial areas, along with a rise in Chemical, Biological, Radioactive, and Nuclear (CBRN) threats around the frontier, including alien fauna attacks. However, the UAAC also wanted a force to monitor and be able to fight in various megacorporations' complexes as insurance if one of the many state-contracted companies decides to go rouge. While all Colonial Marine units are theoretically able to perform combat duties in these environments, their combat ability often fell short due to a lack of CBRN equipment, training, and threat knowledge. The USCM, seemingly lacking the funding and resources to provide these things, instead formed an entirely new company type.
## Welcome to the Suck
HAZOPS platoons are trained to operate almost exclusively in MOPP (Mission Oriented Protective Posture) Level 2 and above, meaning they are always either protected or have protection on-hand for CBRN threats. Their MOPP equipment has been made much more suited to long-term use, including the use of lighter materials, more breathable fabrics, and even small fans and cooling gels installed in overgarments and masks. Additionally, the recently-issued Powered Warfighting Armor has been designed to interface with these systems and provide the user with extended protection, comfort, and computer systems for CBRN threats, though a portion of these armors (Notably the ones issued to the Forth) have been experiencing electrical failures that are causing most features to not be available. HAZOPS has developed a reputation as the “janitors” of the corps, doing jobs nobody else wants to do in environments nobody wants to be in. Training is notoriously difficult, with trainees having to take a 12-month “Hazard Endurance Course” at Fort Santego, including a 2-mile long cross-country run in full Level 4 MOPP. Alongside their standard combat duties, HAZOPS platoons have been known to deploy alongside civilian organizations who need security while operating in especially alien or otherwise CBRN-hazardous environments. These organizations include the DoE, NEST, EPA teams, government or allied research organizations, various survey teams, etcetera.
While historically being armed with mostly standard issue weapons, with a few high-powered flamethrowers and shotguns, the corps has been dumping more and more funding into HAZOPS due to an uptick in corporate research activity and generally more hazardous threats across the frontier. They have begun receiving stockpiles of specially-manufactured experimental weapons, which have been designed or repurposed specifically for use in hazardous environments.
## The Damned Forth
The 4th Hazardous Operations Company, stationed on the USS Mike Vinison alongside a reconnaissance company, was deployed to the Neroid Sector to assist existing allied forces in CBRN combat and noncombat operations within the sector. Unfortunately, like most government forces operating in the Neroid Sector, the Forth are not particularly well maintained. They are riddled with logistics and equipment failures, an example being the Powered Warfighting Armor. While supposedly being equipped with a suite of sensors, countermeasures, warning systems, and even automatic medical procedures, the Forth’s stockpile of PWA has nearly none of these promised features due to a critical electrical fault. The vests have been reduced to their most basic features. While the USCM has promised to either send out technicians to repair the armor or send a new shipment entirely, neither have been accomplished due to both logistical incompetence and supply line troubles, an unfortunately common reason for much of the Forth Company’s troubles. For these reasons, they have been dubbed the “Damned Forth” by allied units who have been deployed with them. The name stuck, and the Forth Company has become proud of the fact that even when faced with insufficient logistical capabilities, they still remain a vital part of UA forces operating in Neroid.
